C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.Name: Windows save pipeline — sandbox prefix check fix plan
C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.IntentSummary: Make m010_security::check_path Windows-honest: a root-only sandbox (the permissive "/" default) admits absolute paths on every platform instead of denying every DOS path; the step-4 lexical prefix comparison strips the \\?\ and \\?\UNC\ device prefixes from both sides; the step-5 symlink comparison skips its prefix denial when the sandbox is the permissive root (canonicalize("/") on Windows is the current-drive root and would falsely deny cross-drive writes) while still returning the canonicalized request. NUL/overlong/lexical-.. /symlink-escape/out-of-sandbox denials all keep holding. Unit tests pin the matrix with Windows-style fixtures; the polygon proves a real disk write through Ctrl+S on the rebuilt NSIS using a scratch document under D:\polygon (the owner's workspace stays read-only).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Two pure helpers land in m010_security.rs: strip_device_prefix(path) removing leading \\?\ and rewriting \\?\UNC\x to \\x, and is_permissive_root(path) true only for a path whose components are at most a RootDir with no drive Prefix and no further components ("/" and "\" — the SecurityCtx::default form on both platforms).

Step 4 compares strip_device_prefix(lexical).starts_with(strip_device_prefix(sandbox_lex)) and is skipped entirely when is_permissive_root(sandbox_lex); the returned validated path stays the unstripped lexical form (callers write to what they asked for).

Step 5 keeps canonicalizing both existing paths and returning req_canon, but its prefix denial only applies when the sandbox is not the permissive root — canonicalize("/") on Windows (current-drive root) must not fence cross-drive writes under the global default.

Every denial keeps firing: NUL, overlong, lexical .. above root, out-of-sandbox DOS/UNC mismatches (a \\?\C:\other request against a \\?\D:\ws sandbox stays PathTraversal), symlink escapes under a real sandbox.

T-002.Title: Unit tests: the Windows fixture matrix

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: New tests pin: permissive_root_default_allows_windows_absolute (sandbox "/", request D:\work\a.md → Ok), unc_sandbox_matches_dos_request (sandbox \\?\D:\ws, request D:\ws\notes.md → Ok), dos_sandbox_matches_unc_request symmetric case, unc_cross_drive_still_denied (\\?\C:\other vs \\?\D:\ws → PathTraversal), traversal_above_root_still_denied, and existing symlink/outside cases stay green.
Fixtures are plain PathBuf::from strings so the suite runs green on every host OS (the helpers are string/component logic, no Windows-only API).

T-003.Title: Graph + verification entries: M-010 / V-M-010 update

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: M-010's summary and interface record the Windows-honest comparison (permissive root, device-prefix strip, step-5 guard); V-M-010 gains the scenario set: the fixture matrix, the unchanged denial suite, and the polygon disk-write proof.

T-004.Title: Polygon acceptance: real disk write through Ctrl+S on the rebuilt NSIS

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Branch NSIS rebuilt on the polygon and silently reinstalled; a scratch document is created under D:\polygon (owner workspace untouched), opened through the mt_open_file channel, dirtied via insertText; real SendInput Ctrl+S → isSaved true, file mtime moves, the probe text round-trips from disk; the README save failure notification no longer appears for workspace files either (permissive default path).
